resources.name: Place order — valid
resources.description:
Happy path. Expect 202 Accepted with the priced OrderResponse.
SKUs come from PriceCatalog: SKU-1 Bookcase 320.99, SKU-2 Shelf 11.99, SKU-3 Wardrobe 33.99.

Check three things in the response:
  * total is 356.96 — 320.99 + (11.99 x 3). If it is 0, nothing is recalculating the total from the lines.
  * items has two entries, each with quantity, unitPrice and lineTotal. The quantity must be what you sent (1 and 3), not the catalogue's own quantity field.
  * orderId is a real persisted id — copy it into the order_id environment variable.

Note: the customerId you send is currently ignored. OrderService hardcodes 'cust-01', which is why the customer_id variable is set to that. Once the id comes from the request (or from a JWT via Spring Security), the variable becomes whatever you send.

resources.name: Place order — fails validation
resources.description:
Blank customerId, lowercase currency (fails the ^[A-Z]{3}$ pattern), quantity 0 (fails @Min(1)) and an empty-ish items list.
Expect 400. Until ORD-003 the body is Spring's default error shape.

resources.name: Place order — unknown SKU
resources.description:
Passes validation, then UnknownSkuException is thrown in the service.
Expect 500 today — turning this into a clean 4xx is the point of ORD-003.

resources.name: Get order by id  [ORD-002 — not built yet]
resources.description: 404s until you add the endpoint. Set the order_id environment variable to an id returned by 'Place order — valid'.

resources.name: List all orders — paged
resources.description:
GET /orders, backed by findAll(Pageable) and mapped to OrderListResponse.

Deliberately has no line items — the javadoc on OrderListResponse explains why: one query per page, and nothing lazy is touched during serialisation.

The page/size/sort params override @PageableDefault(size = 20, sort = 'createdAt', DESC). Sort accepts any OrderEntity property, so 'total,desc' and 'placedAt,asc' both work. Ask for a property that does not exist and you get a 500 from PropertyReferenceException.

resources.name: Get orders by customer — paged, with line items
resources.description:
GET /order?customerId=, backed by the derived query findByCustomerId(String, Pageable) and mapped to OrderResponse — so unlike the list endpoint, each order carries its items.

Requires @RequestParam String customerId on the controller. @PathVariable will fail with MissingPathVariableException, since the path has no {customerId} in it.

Place two or three orders first, then run this. Things worth checking:
  * every order in the page has a populated items array — an empty one means the cascade is not persisting lines
  * no LazyInitializationException — the entity to DTO mapping happens inside @Transactional(readOnly = true), which is what makes touching order.getLines() safe
  * watch the SQL log with spring.jpa.show-sql=true: @BatchSize(50) should fetch the lines for the whole page in one 'where order_id in (...)' rather than one query per order

resources.name: Get orders by customer — no matches
resources.description:
A customer with nothing stored. Expect 200 with an empty content array and totalElements 0 — not a 404.

A collection endpoint that finds nothing has still succeeded; the collection is simply empty. 404 is for a resource that does not exist, which is the get-by-id case.

resources.name: Cancel order  [ORD-002 — not built yet]
resources.description: Should succeed for PENDING and be rejected once OrderStatus.isTerminal() is true.

resources.name: Health
resources.description: Add management.endpoint.health.show-details=always to application.properties to see the 'db' component — the quickest confirmation that Hibernate reached Postgres.
